idiom_name: TypeScript compiler API: forEachChild / visitEachChild / factory update with isX type guards
implementation_notes: The typescript package ships the tree and the transformer: createSourceFile or a program gives the AST, forEachChild performs a read-only walk (the wiki notes it subsumes the visitor pattern), the isX guards (ts.isBinaryExpression and friends) narrow a node, and rewriting uses ts.visitEachChild inside a TransformerFactory with the factory's create and update functions - so the library owns the walk and the rebuild while the rule and the action are your visitor function. Identity is preserved when nothing changes (an update call with unchanged children returns the original node), which makes transforms cheap to compose, and ts.transform plus the printer emits the result. For query-only rules, ESLint selectors or tsquery express the same shapes declaratively without a transformer pipeline.
pitfalls: Hand-rolling the recursion instead of using ts.visitEachChild skips its bookkeeping: updated children keep stale parent pointers and emit-time comments or sourcemaps break.
The AST is immutable and update functions take every argument, so a rule that returns the same node changes nothing - and a rewrite must return the original node when the pattern does not match.
Node identity, not structure, is what the transformer uses to decide whether anything changed, so comparing nodes by text or by == is wrong and forces needless reprinting.
